name_note: GTDB restricts the genus Clostridium to the Clostridium sensu stricto group, so many species historically named Clostridium are classified in other genera.

sentences.text: Clostridium sensu stricto is regarded as the true Clostridium genus and contains important human and animal pathogens as well as industrially relevant bacteria.
The genus as classically defined is phenotypically and genotypically diverse, and many species carrying the name Clostridium fall outside Clostridium sensu stricto.
Clostridium butyricum is described as a butyrate-producing human gut symbiont that has been used as a probiotic for decades.
A review reports that C. butyricum strains have been investigated for potential protective effects across human diseases including inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer.
Clostridium neonatale, a species of Clostridium sensu stricto, was isolated during an outbreak of neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis, and clinical strains came from stools of preterm neonates.
